Lucy turns back toward Nora and presses her palms together.

“Then I’m not going yet. I wanted to finish; I still do. But Regina didn’t keep me on my feet just so I could walk away while her work loses its home.”

She lets her hands fall and remains where she is.

“Leave my name there for now. Ask someone who can actually take it over, and let me know what they agree to do. I’m not promising to stay forever. I’m saying that midnight shouldn’t be allowed to settle this for us. We can find a proper ending without making it the archive’s ending too.”

Lucy listens to the end, then slowly opens her clasped hands.

“June has taken it? Starting now? Then… yes. That’s what I needed to hear.”

She draws back a step and gives Nora a small, embarrassed smile.

“I kept thinking leaving would mean being ungrateful. As though Regina’s work could only stay alive if my name stayed beside it. Please tell June I’m thankful she’s doing this. I would have liked to say it myself.”

Lucy turns toward the way out, then pauses.

“And thank you for checking, Nora. For telling me plainly. I think I can finish now without feeling that I’ve abandoned her.”

Lucy lifts a hand as though to reach out, then draws it back and bows instead.

“Thank you. For the news, and for saying it like that. I can hear it without feeling I’m being pushed out.”

Her outline thins, but the smile remains.

“I wanted to give something back. To her, and now to you. But if I start finding another reason to stay every time somebody is kind, I shall never finish, shall I?”

She clasps her hands once more.

“Then let this be enough: I’m grateful. May someone speak as gently to you when you need it. Please remember that I left relieved.”

Lucy’s smile vanishes. She turns her fading face back toward the cleric.

“I will thank you for the news. I won’t thank you for speaking of her like that. A whole country of worshippers doesn’t make that remark any less small.”

She raises one finger, still drifting away.

“Regina mattered to me when I needed help. You have done something kind today too, which makes that splendid little speech an especially poor use of your mouth.”

A sharp smile returns.

“I am leaving, as I intended. You may keep your good riddance. I’ve heard the useful part, and I don’t need to stay for the rest.”
